definitions.explanation: the sound a phone makes to notify the user of an incoming call or message

examples.japanese: {着信音|ちゃくしんおん}を{変|か}えた。
{電車|でんしゃ}の{中|なか}では{着信音|ちゃくしんおん}を{切|き}ってください。
examples.english: Please turn off your ringtone on the train.

examples.japanese: {好|す}きな{曲|きょく}を{着信音|ちゃくしんおん}に{設定|せってい}した。
examples.english: I set my favorite song as my ringtone.

notes:
Compound of {着信|ちゃくしん} (incoming call/message) + {音|おん} (sound). The standard term for the sound a phone makes when receiving a call or message.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {着信音|ちゃくしんおん}を{変|か}える: to change one's ringtone
- {着信音|ちゃくしんおん}を{切|き}る: to turn off the ringtone
- {着信音|ちゃくしんおん}を{設定|せってい}する: to set a ringtone

SHORTENED FORM:
{着|ちゃく}メロ — a popular abbreviated form, especially for music ringtones. Less common now that smartphones are standard.

RELATED WORDS:
- {通知音|つうちおん}: notification sound
- マナーモード: manner mode (silent/vibration mode, unique to Japanese)
- バイブ: vibration (casual abbreviation of バイブレーション)
